correctness.rationale: For an SPD A with eigenvalues in [mu,L], the delayed Rayleigh quotient r lies in [mu,L], so h=p/r and every spectral product h*lambda is in [p/kappa,p*kappa]. Since p>=1, max(abs(1-p/kappa),abs(1-p*kappa))=p*kappa-1. The same squared modal bound controls Euclidean gradient norm and A^-1-weighted objective gap. In the actual exact-line-search warm-up A=diag(kappa,1), g0=(sqrt(e),1), the next gradient lies in the large-eigenvalue mode as e->0 while h1->p, so both ratios tend to (p*kappa-1)^2, proving a sharp supremum. For p*kappa>2 sufficiently small positive e yields strict increases. Endpoint p*kappa=2 ensures nonincrease, not necessarily exact attainment. Independent rational iterates tested kappa=5/1.5/2 and p=1.5/1.2/1 with multiple scales; universal analytic proof remains separate.
